newsitem.title: FRANCE: No talk of EU economic sanctions on Iran - France.
newsitem.headline: No talk of EU economic sanctions on Iran - France.

text.p: European Union states have not discussed economic sanctions against Iran after a German court ruled that Tehran's rulers ordered the murder of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, a senior French officials said on Friday.

The 15 EU member states, supporting Germany, recalled their ambassadors for consultations and said they saw no room to continue their so-called "critical dialogue" while Iran "flouts international norms and indulges in acts of terrorism."
However the French official suggested the EU was not about to follow a United States call for sanctions against Tehran.
"We only talked about political matters yesterday," the official told Reuters, adding that EU foreign ministers would review relations with Iran when they meet next on April 29.
He noted that the United States was by far Iran's biggest foreign trade customer, while France was in fifth place behind Germany, Italy and Britain.

"Franco-Iranian trade is very slight. Last year, we imported goods worth a little more than six billion francs, 95 percent of which was oil and five percent pistachio nuts and rugs. We sold goods worth three billion francs," he said.
"Our economic interests are very small," the official said.
The United States has warned French oil companies they could fall foul of controversial American legislation punishing firms that supply oil-drilling equipment to Tehran.
France's Total and Elf Aquitaine are at the top of the list of potential targets of a series of sanctions included in the so-called D'Amato act, named after Republican senator Alfonse d'Amato.
The French government announced plans last month to enact countervailing legislation making it an offence for any French company to comply with such a foreign restriction.
